summary: 100 ft Aermotor LS-40 tower; NHLR places it in Issaquena County (Forest Lookouts says Sharkey); vacated by MFC, with an unclear register sentence saying county maintenance uses it; no build date.

facts.design: 100 ft Aermotor LS-40 with an internal straight staircase
facts.status_note: Register notes the bottom flight of stairs has been removed; no later condition found
facts.agency: Issaquena County Maintenance Dept. (register says MFC vacated the site)

events.note: Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register July 10, 2022 as US 1656, MS 22; nominated by Jason Johns
Register records a site visit on 7/8/22; the description at that listing says the bottom flight of stairs has been removed
EF4 tornado struck the town of Rolling Fork on March 24, 2023; it formed in northern Issaquena County; no source read says it reached the lookout

corrections.proposed: Issaquena County Maintenance Dept. (MFC vacated the site)
corrections.why: The register description says the MFC vacated the site and that the Issaquena County Maintenance Dept. now uses it. The register header still says MFC administers it, and Forest Lookouts still lists MFC, so this is a probable stale value, not a settled one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register places the tower in Issaquena County; the Forest Lookouts page for Rolling Fork files it under Sharkey County, where the town of Rolling Fork is. The story keeps the register's county, since the record already uses it and the register gives coordinates for the site. Not settled by any source read.

notes_for_editor: Two register-level sources plus one town article. The register is the only source for the tower itself: location, elevation, 100 ft LS-40 description, build date unknown, a 7/8/22 site visit, stairs removed, and the MFC-to-county handover. One register sentence is garbled ('is now being by the Issaquena County Maintenance Dept.'); the story reads it as 'now uses it' and says the wording is unclear. The county conflict is real: the register and the record say Issaquena; Forest Lookouts says Sharkey, and the town of Rolling Fork is in Sharkey. A GNIS populated-place entry for Rolling Fork (Sharkey County) sits some distance east of the register coordinates; not cited because the GNIS file is a zip the quote checker cannot read. The Wikipedia article was cached as wikitext; only the two tornado sentences are used, and no source says the tower was damaged. No access key set: no source gives an access level, and the register's stairs note and county-use note are not a public-access statement. No staffing, fire history or build date found. Forest Lookouts' Rolling Fork page gives no more detail than county and agency. Story length is set by these thin sources.
